answer: Reciprocal escrow matching. Each new identity must be matched by an existing member who posts a walnut-sized escrow equal to the newcomer's, and pairs are recorded in a shared nebula index that makes every match visible to all members. Because escrows are mutual and time-locked, an attacker inflating the graph must lock real capital per edge and find willing counterparts, so cost scales with connections rather than identities. Any jade-flagged default by one member forfeits both escrows, making each fake identity a liability that drags its sponsor's funds.
